standard_prerequisites.name: Degenerate simplices as compositions of degeneracies
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard description of degenerate simplices: every surjective [n+1] -> [n+1-k] is uniquely sigma^{n-k}_{i_k} ... sigma^n_{i_1} with 0 <= i_1 <= ... <= i_k <= n-k+1

core_obligations: The uniqueness remark (proof lines 2118-2126): d_i s_i = id lets any x in U_{m+1} be written uniquely as x' + x'' with d_i(x') = 0 and x'' = s_i(z) in the image of s_i (x' = x - s_i(d_i(x)), s_i injective).

The decomposition procedure and the kernel claim (lines 2128-2185): recursively strip off s_0(z_0), ..., s_n(z_n) with d_i(x_i) = 0 at each stage; ascending induction on i shows x_i lies in the intersection of ker(d_0)..ker(d_i) and z_i in ker(d_0)..ker(d_{i-1}) - the step uses the simplicial relations to rewrite d_j(x_{i-1}) = d_j(x_i) + s_{i-1}(d_j(z_i)) and the uniqueness remark to force both terms zero; the base case i = 0 is definitional (the author's 'This is clear for n = 0' opens the outer induction with N(U_0) = U_0).

The direct-sum decomposition (lines 2187-2205): the claim reorganizes into U_{n+1} = N(U_{n+1}) + the sum of s_i(ker d_0 .. ker d_{i-1}), with the kernels of initial segments identified as partial sums; iterating the decomposition of each z_i produces the normal form x = sum s_{i_1}...s_{i_k}(z) with 0 <= i_1 <= ... <= i_k <= n-k+1 and z in N(U_{n+1-k}), matching the unique factorization of surjections [n+1] -> [n+1-k] as sigma^{n-k}_{i_k} ... sigma^n_{i_1} - exactly the required splitting for m <= n, completing the induction.
proof_roadmap: Establish the uniqueness remark d_i s_i = id splitting each level.
Run the stripping procedure and prove by induction the kernel memberships of the remainders.
Reassemble as the direct-sum decomposition and iterate to the degenerate-simplex normal form.
